newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Siberian snow seen negative for grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Siberian snow seen negative for grain harvest.

text.p: A cold front and snow flurries headed for Siberia over the next 10 days will decrease grain yields slightly in the region but the harvest will continue at close to normal levels, a Russian forecaster said on Friday.
Viktor Trenin of the State Meteorological Service said freezing weather had hit Siberia, especially in grain-rich Altai region, where daytime temperatures have edged to minus five degrees Celsius.
"The combines will continue to harvest, but grain losses will mount," he said.
But he said the losses would still be small as the large machines ploughed through light snowfalls. The harvest is lagging by about two weeks.
"Through the middle of the month we expect the harvest to continue under normal conditions," he said, adding he had no predictions for what might happen later.
Trenin said flurries would occasionally hamper the efficiency of the combines but grain quality would not be affected by the cold weather.
Independent agricultural analyst Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd said quality would fall.
"Grain is not like watermelons, but the quality of the grain suffers in sub-zero temperature -- the quality will be worse."
He said the biggest problem would be if Siberia warmed up and rain fell, followed by renewed cold.
"If there was rain followed by frost, the combines would have a hard time harvesting the grain," he said.
Trenin said it was too early to forecast when snows would lie deep enough to end the harvest and said he was not ready to say whether grain would be left in the fields.

Sizov said in northern regions of Siberian grain centres Omsk and Novosibirsk some grain would not be gathered, and he predicted western Siberia's harvest would be about 9.4 million tonnes, out of a total 67-69 million tonnes. --Peter Henderson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
